title.narrative: EDUCATION AND TRAINING FOR EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT

description.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire - EDUCATION AND TRAINING FOR EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT: The Skills for Employability and Productivity Project will increase access to secondary education and teacher training, and support the construction of up to 84 new secondary schools. Through a public-private partnership, a new technical vocational education and training (TVET) model will advance development of in-demand skills. It will also help the government mitigate gender disparities, improving outcomes for girls in the education system.

title.narrative: Students benefitting from improved teacher training

description.narrative: Level Outcome of According to Annex II of the Monitoring and Evaluation Plan, this indicator was to be reported for the first time in year 6 (July 24 to August 25) of the Compact. The student teachers trained on the new curriculum completed their training in July 2024. To collect this indicator, it is necessary to have the distribution of 966 bivalent teachers throughout the country and then determine the number of students taught by each of them in their schools of assignment. Due to the logistical difficulties related to the data collection process throughout the country, the time remaining before the Compact closing and the fact that the Boussole platform to track teachers is not yet used at the national level, this indicator could not be calculated. Therefore, no data will be reported for this indicator by the end of the Compact.

title.narrative: Educational facilities constructed or rehabilitated

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of According to the TVET Activity work plans and Annex II of the M&E Plan, reporting on this indicator was expected to start during year 5 of the compact, following completion of the construction of the TVET centers. In order to be considered fully constructed and ready to receive students, a TVET center must not only have completed major works but also be equipped, have all utilities connected, and comply with relevant MCC and national policies regarding safety and security. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic combined with delays in implementation of the TVET Activity (delays and challenges with the process to select and sign agreements with the private sector consortia, delays in procuring construction works, etc.), the construction of the TVET centers did not begin until 2024 and will not be completed until after the end of the compact, with the first cohorts of students expected to enroll in 2026. This indicator will be reported on as part of the independent evaluation of the TVET Activity, with the final evaluation report expected in 2030.

title.narrative: Lower-secondary schools substantially completed

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of Initially, the Compact planned for at least 74 lower-secondary schools to be substantially completed. The target of 74 lower-secondary schools was not reached due to an increase in school construction costs and delays related, among other reasons, to the COVID-19 pandemic. In August 2024, a Compact modification was approved that finalized the scope of lower-secondary school construction at 40 schools. The M&E Plan states that this indicator will count schools when they are "sufficiently completed in accordance with the construction contract documents, so that classrooms and other facilities can be used for the intended purpose." The required source document is the construction completion certificate. By the end of the compact, source documents were signed and available for 36 of the 40 schools. At Compact End Date (CED), however, for several of the schools, the construction works were not substantially completed. Thus, 36 is likely an overestimate of the number of educational facilities ready for the first day of classes by CED, as per the definition set forth in the M&E Plan.

title.narrative: Classrooms constructed and ready for use

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of Initially, the Compact planned for the construction of 752 classrooms. This target was not reached due to an increase in school construction costs and delays related, among other reasons, to the COVID-19 pandemic. In August 2024, a Compact modification was approved that finalized the scope of lower-secondary school construction at 496 classrooms within 40 schools. The M&E Plan states that this indicator will count classrooms when schools are completely equipped and prepared for the first day of classes. The required source documents include construction completion certificates, equipment delivery receipts, and utility connection certificates. By the end of the compact, source documents were signed and available for 36 of the 40 schools. At Compact End Date (CED), however, for several of the schools, the construction works were not substantially completed, and staff furniture and student desks were still being assembled. Thus, 440 is likely an overestimate of the number of classrooms ready for the first day of classes by CED, as per the definition set forth in the M&E Plan.

title.narrative: Gross enrollment rate for school-aged children in the catchment areas of Compact-supported lower-secondary schools

description.narrative: Level Outcome of This indicator is defined as the proportion of children enrolled in Compact-supported lower-secondary schools over the population of children of the official age (12-15 years) to be enrolled in lower-secondary school. For the numerator, the first set of 13 lower-secondary schools (CDPs) were completed in the fall of 2024 and enrolled 873 students in the first year of lower secondary school (6th). However, the denominator for this indicator - population of children of the official age to be enrolled in lower-secondary school - was not available for the 2024-2025 school year and therefore this indicator could not be calculated. That being said, during the previous school year 2023-2024, 44,330 students were enrolled in the last year of primary school (CM2) in all the villages of the Compact catchment areas. Using this figure, the gross enrollment rate can be estimated at around 2% for the 2024-2025 school year.

That being said, during the previous school year 2023-2024, 44,330 students were enrolled in the last year of primary school (CM2) in all the villages of the Compact catchment areas.
